meaning: A work works if, as rendered, it shows a reader something true and legible about White's letters and their seasons: it draws completely, fits its frame, its marks and labels stay readable and attached to what they label, and its key matches what is drawn.

items.why: A complete, legible calendar wheel of letters and the creatures and weather each month names, with a clear key, that turns White's twenty years into one Selborne year.
The spiral of dated letters, with Pennant and Barrington told apart, undated letters listed at the sides and one keyword per spoke, draws cleanly and does what its caption says.
The spiral is drawn too large for the frame, so its outer turns are cut off at top and bottom and run under the labels and side lists.
Same sound spiral as W02; one subtitle line is shifted left out of alignment, a cosmetic slip that does not hide or misstate anything.
The picture is a blank cream page with nothing rendered.
Labels have come loose from their spokes and pile onto each other (for example 'missel-thrush' printed over 'swifts'), so you cannot tell which word belongs to which letter.

A legible month wheel whose word clouds and inner sentence tally show what lived in each month of the letters, with an honest key and note.

Every dated letter is placed on its day in a year spiral and labelled with its opening words, with White's own quote about the Annus Historico-naturalis explaining the idea, and it is clean and readable.
Letters in book order are threaded down to the dates they were written, so the book's reordering of the correspondence is clear and legibly drawn.
Each month gathers the actual passages that name it, an Annus Historico-naturalis built from White's own words, and the dense text stays readable and well ordered.
Letters are placed on their writing day and threaded to the months they speak of, with side lists for undated letters and most-named months, and everything reads clearly.
